documents.title: TerraLeb Privacy Notice
documents.summary: Owner-reviewed Lebanon v1 draft. Production serves it only after verified operator details and counsel approval are attached to this exact text.

sections.heading: Who operates TerraLeb
paragraphs: TerraLeb is intended for a Lebanon-based operator. The verified legal name, legal form or authority, serviceable address, monitored privacy contact and accountable owner must be inserted from the signed release record before this notice can be published in production. TerraLeb does not attribute this role to NCRS, CNRS, a ministry, municipality, company or individual without evidence.

sections.heading: Data processed
paragraphs: TerraLeb can process account/contact information, roles and assignments, precise GIS geometry and accuracy, field photos, form attributes, comments/reviews, imports/exports, AI run and validation records, notifications/device tokens, sessions, and security/audit records.

sections.heading: Purposes and choices
paragraphs: Required service processing protects accounts, enforces roles and project visibility, operates assigned institutional workflows, and records necessary security and audit evidence. Precise geometry, photos, comments, imports, exports and offline storage occur only when an authorized user deliberately uses those features. Push notifications are optional. Public publication requires a separate project authority decision.
bullets: AI is disabled for every project by default and is controlled by the protected super administrator. Its inputs are approved project GIS data and imagery, not account profiles, contact details, credentials, sessions, device tokens, notifications, unrelated projects or private drafts.
General, unrelated or cross-project AI training is prohibited in v1.
The final notice must state the counsel-approved legal basis for each active purpose; this owner draft does not label every purpose as consent.

sections.heading: Recipients and locations
paragraphs: Authorized project personnel receive only data permitted by their role. The current hosting candidate is DigitalOcean Frankfurt, Germany, using a private production Droplet and private Spaces object storage. This is an international hosting location for a Lebanon-only service and remains blocked until the operator accepts the provider terms, transfer assessment and exact deployment evidence. Conditional providers are a contracted SMTP service, Firebase Cloud Messaging, ArcGIS online maps and an approved Earth Engine plan.
bullets: Phone numbers are format-validated only; no SMS provider is used in v1.
No advertising or behavioral analytics SDK is used in v1.
Map providers can receive requested tile coordinates, IP/network and client metadata; displaying a basemap does not upload a user's account profile to the map provider.

sections.heading: Retention and deletion
paragraphs: The owner schedule uses short operational retention, including 24 hours for encrypted personal-data export artifacts, 7 days for ordinary project export files, 30 days for routine logs and temporary imports, 35 days for backups, 90 days for inactive drafts or rejected/private photos, and 180 days for notifications. Accepted institutional GIS and minimum provenance may remain through the active project and for the approved review period described in the current retention register.
bullets: Deactivation is not deletion.

Completed deletion erases credentials, contact and private account data, sessions, device tokens, drafts and pending or unapproved content. Accepted GIS and minimum approved institutional provenance can remain under a pseudonymous masked label for authorized users; public output uses Contributor. A masked label is not legal anonymity.

Backups expire naturally and a deletion ledger prevents erased identities from being restored into active state. A legal hold is disabled unless a specific protected, expiring and audited hold is approved.

sections.heading: Your choices and requests
paragraphs: Users can request a copy of their personal data, correction, restriction or objection review, and reviewed account deletion from the app. Requests are authenticated, rate-limited, tracked and visible to the requester. A public deletion-request route does not reveal whether an account exists.
bullets: Permission for camera, photos and notifications is requested contextually when the related feature is used.
Disabling push notifications does not disable authenticated in-app notifications.
The verified public privacy contact and applicable complaint route must be inserted before production publication.

sections.heading: Security
paragraphs: TerraLeb uses role-based access, session controls, private media routes, encrypted owner-scoped offline storage, audit controls, private object storage and protected transport in production. No system can guarantee absolute security.

documents.title: TerraLeb Terms of Use
documents.summary: Owner-reviewed terms for Lebanon v1. Verified operator facts and counsel approval are required before production publication.

sections.heading: Eligibility and accounts
paragraphs: TerraLeb v1 is offered and targeted in Lebanon to users aged 18 or older. Minors may not create or use accounts. Users must provide accurate account information, protect credentials, and use only roles and projects they are authorized to access. The verified operator identity, governing-law and dispute wording will be inserted only from the signed release record.

sections.heading: Field work and contributed content
paragraphs: Users must have authority to enter property, collect locations, take or upload photos, import third-party data and share it with the assigned project. Users must provide source, licence, attribution, accuracy and redistribution information when required.
bullets: A contributor keeps rights they actually hold and grants the operator and responsible project institution the non-exclusive rights needed to receive, store, secure, validate, transform for GIS interoperability, review, use in the approved project AI workflow, back up and export accepted contributions.
Publication requires a separate institutional authority and protected-super-admin decision. Signup acceptance does not authorize public publication.

The operational permission for an accepted official record survives deletion only for the approved retention period. TerraLeb does not claim ownership of third-party or institutional data merely because it was uploaded.

sections.heading: Review, accuracy and service limitations
paragraphs: Submissions, imports, exports and AI-derived layers may require review. Offline data can be stale and synchronization can conflict. Users must verify critical decisions against authoritative sources.

sections.heading: Suspension, deactivation and deletion
paragraphs: Security and project rules can restrict access. Contributor deactivation is reversible and distinct from deletion. Every role except the protected super administrator may submit a reviewed deletion request. A protected administrator may explicitly discard unfinished work and release or transfer responsibilities. Completed deletion erases direct identifiers, credentials, private data, drafts and pending or unapproved records; accepted GIS and minimum institutional provenance may remain for the approved period under masked internal attribution, while public output uses Contributor.

sections.heading: Availability, responsibility and changes
paragraphs: TerraLeb is provided for authorized project work and may be interrupted for maintenance, security, provider outages or legal requirements. It does not guarantee cadastral, survey, emergency-navigation, GPS, imagery or AI accuracy. Users must verify critical decisions with an authoritative source.
bullets: Nothing in the final Terms may exclude liability or rights that applicable law does not permit the operator to exclude.
Users remain responsible for lawful field access, photography, source rights and compliance with project instructions.

Material Terms or Acceptable Use changes require a new affirmative acceptance. The intended owner notice is 30 days where practical; urgent security or legal changes may take effect sooner with a clear notice.
Reports and takedown requests use the in-app workflow or verified public contact. Final warranty, limitation, indemnity, governing-law and dispute clauses require counsel approval before publication.

documents.title: TerraLeb Acceptable Use Policy
documents.summary: Owner-reviewed safety and content rules for the Lebanon v1 release; final counsel approval is required.

sections.heading: Prohibited conduct
paragraphs: Do not bypass authorization, interfere with the service, upload malware, harass people, impersonate others, scrape protected data, or use TerraLeb for unlawful surveillance or discrimination.

sections.heading: Content and location safety
paragraphs: Do not upload unlawful, abusive, deceptive, infringing or unnecessary personal content. Do not publish sensitive sites, private-property details, faces or identifying evidence without authority.

sections.heading: Data and map sources
paragraphs: Do not import, export or redistribute data without the required rights, attribution and restrictions. Do not use TerraLeb to evade map-provider limits or licenses.

sections.heading: Reporting and enforcement
paragraphs: Use Report project content or the verified public support channel for harmful, unlawful, infringing or unauthorized material. A report does not automatically hide or delete content.
bullets: The protected moderation queue records the original report, status, responsible administrator, action and response.
TerraLeb targets an initial review within 10 calendar days and expedites credible safety, security or unlawful-disclosure reports.
Actions use existing authoritative correction, restriction, unpublication and escalation workflows. A user may request further review through the same tracked case or verified support channel.
The final operator must publish an emergency/escalation route; TerraLeb is not an emergency service.

documents.title: TerraLeb Important GIS and AI Notices
documents.summary: Owner-reviewed field, map and AI safety notices; final counsel approval is required before production publication.

sections.heading: Not an authoritative boundary or survey
paragraphs: TerraLeb maps, geometries and measurements are not cadastral records, land-title evidence, legal boundaries or a professional survey unless an authorized body explicitly certifies a named output.

sections.heading: Not emergency navigation
paragraphs: Do not rely on TerraLeb for emergency response, personal safety, navigation or other time-critical decisions.

sections.heading: Accuracy and staleness
paragraphs: GPS accuracy, imagery dates, imported data, offline packages and AI predictions vary and can be incomplete or wrong. Confirm synchronization and review/publication state.

sections.heading: Field and publication responsibility
paragraphs: Obtain authority for property access, photography, collection, import, export and publication. Do not disclose sensitive locations without the responsible authority's approval.

sections.heading: Source terms
paragraphs: Basemaps, imagery and imported datasets retain their own licenses, attribution and redistribution limits.

documents.title: Request TerraLeb Account Deletion
documents.summary: Every user except the protected super administrator can initiate and track a reviewed deletion request. Production execution remains fail-closed until the approved policy evidence is configured.

sections.heading: How to request deletion
paragraphs: Sign in, open Profile, find Account access, choose Request account deletion, review the notice and confirm with your current password. Every role except the protected super administrator can initiate a request. If you cannot sign in, use /legal/account-deletion/request; that public form does not confirm whether an account exists and requires identity verification before action. The approved privacy contact must also be published before release.

sections.heading: Review and responsibilities
paragraphs: A contributor or administrator may submit a request at any time. The protected administrator reviews assignments, queued work and institutional responsibilities. The administrator must explicitly choose whether unfinished work is resolved or permanently discarded and whether responsibilities are released or transferred. No destructive choice is preselected. The user may cancel while the request is pending verification, submitted or in review, but not after it is scheduled or processing.

sections.heading: What is deleted
paragraphs: Completed deletion removes the password and credentials, email, phone, verification/recovery state, sessions, device tokens, notification destinations, private profile fields, the affected owner's local account cache, personal export artifacts, drafts, pending/unapproved work and unnecessary attachments. The account becomes permanently non-authenticatable and cannot be reactivated.

sections.heading: What may remain
paragraphs: Accepted GIS and only the minimum approved review, source, import, publication or AI-validation provenance needed for institutional integrity may remain for the retention period. Internal attribution uses a one-time Unicode-safe pseudonymous masked label such as A. H. for authorized users; public/general output uses Contributor. The full name is not retained to recreate the label, and internal UUIDs are not public identifiers.
bullets: Rejected/private photos are deleted after their shorter period. Accepted photos and exact location follow the accepted record's sensitivity and retention decision and are not published automatically.
Structured identity snapshots are scrubbed. Free text is not silently rewritten; possible identifiers create a restricted review task.
Backups expire after 35 days and a deletion ledger prevents erased identity from returning to active state. A case-specific legal hold must be separately approved, encrypted, expiring and audited.
The requester receives tracked status and a completion or safe failure response. The verified privacy contact will be published before production.

documents.title: TerraLeb Service Providers
documents.summary: Owner-selected service categories for Lebanon v1. Exact active provider entities and effective dates are published only after contract and deployment verification.

sections.heading: Selected production services
paragraphs: The current hosting candidate is DigitalOcean Frankfurt, Germany, with private PostgreSQL on the production Droplet and private purpose-separated Spaces buckets. It is not an approved active subprocessor until account, terms, DPA, region, access and deployment evidence are recorded. Conditional external services are a contracted SMTP provider, Firebase Cloud Messaging, ArcGIS online basemaps and an approved Earth Engine plan. OpenStreetMap Foundation supplies the modest interactive Street tile service. No SMS, advertising or behavioral analytics provider is used in v1.
bullets: The exact contracting legal entity, purpose, data, region, safeguards, effective date and change-notice process for each active provider must be copied from executed records before this page is approved.
The final page lists only services actually enabled in the deployed configuration.
Provider changes require inventory, security, transfer, notice and store-disclosure review before activation.

documents.title: Open-source and Data-source Notices
documents.summary: TerraLeb presents bundled Flutter notices and release-specific backend/container dependency inventories. Final release evidence includes a reviewed SBOM and source attribution.

sections.heading: Software
paragraphs: TerraLeb includes open-source software subject to its authors' license terms. Use the in-app software licenses view for Flutter packages and consult the release SBOM for backend/container components.

sections.heading: Maps and data
paragraphs: OpenStreetMap, Esri, satellite and imported datasets have separate attribution and usage rules that are not replaced by software licenses.
bullets: OpenStreetMap data/copyright: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
Esri legal information: https://www.esri.com/legal
